title: question-tree-embeddings-generator
owner: CC gates writes to cairn/tools/tree/ (charter's gated_by).
intention: A single embeddings generator that takes a question or list of questions. Each device or domain has its own question list. One global question list object holds tuples of (question, owner), self-populating instances in init. Questions persist across sessions and can be removed (e.g., at end of a research run). Two devices can ask the same question — no deduplication, because each job gets its own spin on the data.
why: The root tree 'what questions to ask in the face of novelty' is itself a graph-tree node — the questions are structured knowledge living in the same system they populate. This is inference compilation applied to the question-asking itself (Telos 1). Each question is a render_method; the schema already supports it (trees.py); this builds the producer.
traces_to: Telos 1 — inference compilation: the system learns what questions to ask in the face of novelty.
Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel: established questions are constants, not re-derived each time.
Design: cross-domain-structural-embeddings — HOW THINGS WORK, not surface similarity; multiple render_methods.

falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) the generator cannot accept a single question or a list; (2) two devices asking the same question get deduplicated — they should not, each gets its own spin; (3) a question added for research survives past the research run's explicit removal; (4) a misspelled constant compiles — the constants must be a list of strings that prevents this; (5) the meta-tier (questions about what questions to ask) is not representable in the same structure.

children: none for now — the generator, the global list, and the render_method integration are one mechanism

questions.a: (1) Two devices CAN ask the same question — no deduplication. Each job gets its own spin on the data.
(2) Constants are strings to prevent misspelling. Free-form means temporary questions with a terminal end.
(3) Two tiers: the questions, and the questions to ask to learn what questions to ask.
(4) Questions are not session-limited — they persist until explicitly removed.

how: One global question list object: list of (question, owner) tuples. Self-populating in init — each device/domain registers its questions. Constants for established questions are a list of strings (prevents misspelling). Free-form questions are temporary — added for research with a terminal end, removed when the run completes. Two tiers of novelty: (1) the questions themselves, (2) the questions to ask to learn what questions to ask (meta-questions). Each question is a render_method passed to the embeddings generator.
